documents.title: Student Code of Conduct (academic misconduct provisions naming artificial intelligence)
documents.summary: The Student Code of Conduct defines academic misconduct and names artificial intelligence in its cheating and collusion examples. It sets no positive AI rules; unauthorized AI use counts as misconduct, and what is authorized is left to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The Code says AI is cheating when "not authorized" and that faculty may prohibit behavior in "the course syllabus or class discussion", so it sets no permission or ban itself and leaves authorization to instructors: delegates.

units.why: The Cheating definition says "unauthorized materials, information, notes, study aids or other devices (including artificial intelligence)", so unauthorized AI is cheating and a student-binding ban. P36 fits because it classifies AI misuse as misconduct; it is not P19 since it covers any exercise, not only submitted work.
units.anchor: unauthorized materials, information, notes, study aids or other devices (including artificial intelligence)
units.frag_start: using, attempting to use, or acquiring

units.why: The example "artificial intelligence software) when these are not authorized" shows the Code treats AI as banned unless authorized. I chose P06 (unauthorized means not allowed) over P36 because the point is the default when no authorization exists; fit is partial since it does not mention syllabi.
units.anchor: or artificial intelligence software) when these are not authorized
units.frag_start: Using books, notes or other devices
units.policy: Using artificial intelligence software when it is not authorized is cheating.
units.fit_note: Does not mention a silent syllabus; AI is cheating only when not authorized, implying the default is not allowed.

units.why: The Collusion example "Receiving unauthorized assistance from a source such as software or artificial intelligence" names AI as an illegitimate helper, so it is a misconduct classification (P36).
units.anchor: Receiving unauthorized assistance from a source such as software or artificial intelligence.

units.why: The Fabrication example "Generation of false data by use of software or online means" bans falsified data made with software; AI is not named but generative tools are plausibly covered. P74 is nearest (fabricating data) with a fit note.
units.anchor: Generation of false data by use of software or online means.
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; refers to software or online means generally.

units.why: The sentence "Any behavior specifically prohibited by a faculty member in the course syllabus or class discussion may be considered as academic misconduct" lets instructors set their own prohibitions, which would include AI. P04 fits since the rule is set per instructor.

units.frag_end: may be considered as academic misconduct.
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; general rule that instructor prohibitions count as misconduct.

units.why: The Code states "allegations of academic misconduct will be adjudicated through the proceedings described in University Procedure 13.02.99.C0.04", the formal process that applies to AI-related misconduct. P81 fits as procedure rather than classification.

notes: Only three lines name AI; other units are adjacent misconduct provisions that apply to AI. No other university-level AI document was included.
